question: Should OpenClaw Core own a Pi-to-Review-to-Git-promotion orchestration product and its vendored contracts runtime, or should this workflow remain outside Core behind existing Task Flow and plugin/owner seams?
rationale: This choice defines a new permanent Core responsibility, external-service contract, and supply-chain boundary; it cannot be safely resolved by a mechanical contributor repair.

options.title: Keep the workflow outside Core
options.body: Use the existing Task Flow substrate through an owner plugin or external platform integration, and remove the service-specific orchestration and vendored runtime from this PR.

options.title: Sponsor a Core platform boundary
options.body: Assign an owner to specify the generic Core API, lifecycle, compatibility, source-audit, and security-review requirements before accepting a narrower implementation.

recommendation.title: Keep the workflow outside Core
recommendation.body: Use the existing Task Flow substrate through an owner plugin or external platform integration, and remove the service-specific orchestration and vendored runtime from this PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposed implementation builds directly on the Task Flow subsystem whose durable-state and managed-flow history is the closest relevant ownership trail.
